title: Per-model PTQ profile slate and safety contract for FP8/INT8 rollouts
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Establish a formal per-model post-training quantization (PTQ) profile slate and a safety contract for rolling FP8/INT8 defaults into the model catalog. Deliverables: canonical profile vector for each supported model, a reproducible calibration workflow, CI gating thresholds, and an operational fallback chain that minimizes customer-visible regressions.
motivation: Customers need predictable inference unit economics without unexpected accuracy regressions. Prior runs show large variance between models and datasets; a single global quant default leads to regressions for some model families. This ticket produces curated, auditable per-model PTQ recommendations and the guardrails required to safely serve them across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
calibration_workflow: Stage 1: Dataset fingerprinting - sample representative prompts per workload and compute token length and distribution stats.
Stage 2: Per-layer scale search - run fast histogram-based scale search and two-pass symmetric/asymmetric calibrations for activations.
Stage 3: A/B PTQ variants - generate 3 candidate profiles: conservative INT8 (per-channel), balanced FP8 hybrid, aggressive INT8+group-wise fallback.

Stage 4: Shadow evaluation - run the candidate profiles in shadow against baseline float on 8 evaluation slices: perplexity, instruction-following, instruction-EM, chat-turn coherence, hallucination probes, toxicity, latency, and memory footprint.
Stage 5: Stochastic rounding probe (optional) - use single-run stochastic rounding to estimate worst-case variance for FP8 paths.
Stage 6: Acceptance decision - pick profile that meets safety contract or escalate to QAT/hand-tuning.
Artifacts: calibration job scripts, deterministic seeds, and exportable profile YAML per model.
validation_plan: Metric baselines: define float32 baseline for each metric and compute relative delta.
Primary signal: task-specific accuracy (classification/EM) and instruction-following score measured on curated prompt sets.
Secondary signals: token-level logprob KL divergence, perplexity ratio, and distributional drift on hidden activations.
Thresholds: <=1.5% relative drop on primary metrics OR within 95th percentile of historical model noise; token-logprob KL < 0.02; perplexity ratio <=1.05.
Stability checks: 10 repeated seeds, 3 dataset slices, and long-run 24h stress sampling to detect mode collapse or rare failures.
Human review: for any candidate where primary delta is between 1.0%-1.5%, run a 5-person SME review and collect granular failure cases.
CI gating: profiles must pass an automated job and produce an artifact stored in the artifact registry with provenance metadata.
Regression windows: weekly run for first 3 weeks of rollout, then biweekly for next 9 weeks.
Reporting: generate a per-profile validation report summarizing pass/fail reasons and recommended fallback chain.
acceptance_criteria: Each model in scope has a primary recommended profile (FP8-hybrid / INT8-per-channel / INT8-group) and a documented fallback path.
Recommended profile meets all validation thresholds and produces an artifact with reproducible seeds and calibration inputs.
CI gating job exists and is green; PR that updates model-catalog entries includes the validation report link.
Console surfaces per-model recommended profile and a toggle to opt models into the rollout with one-click canary.
Rollback policy defined: automatic rollback on >= 3% downstream user error-rate increase or sustained metric drift outside thresholds for 1 hour.
Documentation: Confluence runbook for debugging calibration failures and checklist for private deployment upgrade.
Security review completed and KMS keys used for any sensitive sample logging are configured.
rollout_strategy: Stage A: internal canary - run traffic for internal tenants 0.5% of production with monitoring hooks for all primary/secondary signals.
Stage B: contract customers opt-in - enable via console toggles for customers with dedicated capacity and agreed SLAs.
Stage C: gradual ramp - 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with evaluation windows at each step and automated roll/fallthrough to float or alternate profile.
Stage D: full catalog update - annotate model-catalog defaults and publish validation reports and rollback triggers.
Fallback chains: FP8 -> INT8 per-channel -> FP16 (soft-fallback) -> float baseline (hard-fallback).
Observability: per-profile dashboards for token cost savings, 99th percentile latency delta, and customer-facing quality regressions.
Manual gates: SME sign-off required before moving beyond 20% ramp for models classified as high-risk.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Edge-case hallucinations increase with aggressive quant. Mitigation: include targeted hallucination probes in evaluation and require human review for any positive signal.
Risk: Silent distributional drift on private datasets. Mitigation: customers can enable local shadowing and opt-out; provide local calibration runner.
Risk: CI flakiness due to nondeterministic PTQ ops. Mitigation: pin seeds, containerize calibration image, and store hash of calibration input sample.
Risk: Performance regression on small-batch latency-sensitive workloads. Mitigation: runtime exposes profile-specific batch and kernel knobs; recommend per-route overrides in console.
Risk: Security - sample leakage in calibration logs. Mitigation: PII redaction, token-truncation, and enforce KMS encryption for any stored samples.
